title: Speaker urges Bihari diaspora in Sydney to invest for state’s devpt - The Times of India
full_text:
Speaker urges Bihari diaspora in Sydney to invest for state’s devpt
He highlighted investment opportunities in industries, agriculture, education, healthcare, skill development and entrepreneurship, and said initiatives such as Single Window Clearance, SIPDB and the Bihar Industrial Investment Promotion Package (BIIPP)-2025 were intended to facilitate investment and create employment.
Kumar also pointed to emerging opportunities under various state policies in sectors including semiconductors, IT, electronics, biofuels, textiles, leather, food processing and renewable energy.
Kumar said professionals from the state settled abroad could contribute not only capital but also technical expertise, managerial experience and international networks. Their involvement, he said, could help develop skills among Bihar’s youth, promote startups, expand markets for local products and generate employment.
The Speaker urged the diaspora to build sustained partnerships with institutions and businesses in Bihar instead of limiting their connection to cultural and emotional ties.

title: Palamu police seize 9.66 kgs of opium, two held - The Times of India
full_text:
Palamu police seize 9.66 kgs of opium, two held
Acting on the tip-off, Chhaterpur SDPO Prashant Kumar launched vehicle checking on the Chhaterpur-Japla road. During the operation, police intercepted a Bihar-registered motorcycle and arrested its rider, identified as Ranjan Rajak (36), a resident of Gaya district in Bihar.
Police recovered 2.66kg of opium from Rajak, who had allegedly travelled from Bihar to Chhaterpur to procure the contraband, SDPO Kumar said.
“Based on the information provided by Rajak, police raided the house of a local resident, Dayanand Prasad (60), and recovered another 7kg of opium,” Kumar said.
Both Rajak and Prasad have been arrested and further investigation is underway to establish the source of the opium and identify others involved in the alleged supply network, police said.

title: Uprooted trees disrupt traffic as rain batters south Odisha - The Times of India
full_text:
Uprooted trees disrupt traffic as rain batters south Odisha
Fire service personnel rushed to the affected locations and removed the trees, restoring road communication. Traffic between Samantiapalli and Ichhapuram in neighbouring Andhra Pradesh resumed after emergency teams cleared the blockade. “Our teams reached the sites immediately after the trees fell on the road and restored traffic movement,” said Thakur Prasad Dalai, fire officer. BDO (Patrapur) Laxman Soren said connectivity on all affected roads has been restored.
With the weather system expected to bring more heavy rainfall, the district administrations of Ganjam and Gajapati districts have stepped up preparedness. Officials said people living in kutcha houses and vulnerable areas are likely to be shifted to safer locations if the situation worsens.
As a precautionary measure, schools and anganwadi centres in both districts have been closed from Tuesday to Thursday. Officials have also intensified awareness campaigns in vulnerable villages, urging people to move to safer places if required.
Collector (Ganjam) Keerthi Vasan V said all 110 cyclone shelters in the district have been kept ready. Schools and community centres will be used as temporary shelters if evacuation becomes necessary. “We have activated control rooms in all blocks, tehsils and urban local bodies. Their contact numbers have been circulated, and people have been asked to report any emergency immediately,” the collector said.
In Gajapati district, the administration has focused on landslide-prone and remote areas. Asha and anganwadi workers have been using public address systems to alert residents and advise them to remain prepared for evacuation. Pregnant women in vulnerable locations have also been shifted to nearby healthcare facilities as a precautionary measure.

title: Admin to launch drive for 100% Abha card coverage - The Times of India
full_text:
Admin to launch drive for 100% Abha card coverage
At PDS shops, beneficiaries coming to collect ration will be informed about Abha cards and assisted in creating them through the Abha app. PDS dealers have been asked to play an active role in the drive.
Anganwadi workers and helpers will facilitate Abha card creation during village health, sanitation and nutrition days and take-home ration days. The district education officer has been directed to facilitate Abha card creation for students in schools.
The campaign will also cover Jeevika Didis and their family members. Jeevika Didis and ASHA workers will undertake door-to-door outreach to inform residents about Abha and the digital health system.
The DM also directed Sahaj Vasudha Kendras to facilitate Abha card creation for citizens visiting Common Service Centres. Officials have been asked to regularly review the campaign and work in a coordinated, mission-mode manner.

title: Govt mulls restoring 27% OBC quota in next yr’s panchayat polls - The Times of India
full_text:
Govt mulls restoring 27% OBC quota in next yr’s panchayat polls
“The matter of providing reservation to OBCs/socially and economically backward classes (SEBCs) in the upcoming panchayat election is under examination by the state govt,” Naik said in the assembly.
In a written response to a question by BJD MLA Ranendra Pratap Swain, Naik said, “The state had to amend Orissa Grama Panchayat Act, 1964, Orissa Panchayat Samiti Act, 1959, and Orissa Zilla Parishad Act, 1991 in 2021 following SC’s “triple test” mandate in the K Krishna Murthy case and subsequent directions of Orissa high court. The amendments capped the combined reservation for SCs, STs and OBCs at 50%, impacting the earlier provision of 27% reservation for OBCs/SEBCs.”
In Dec 2021, the high court had directed the state election commission to conduct panchayat polls without OBC reservation after observing that the state had failed to furnish empirical data to justify the quantum of quota for backward classes. Consequently, the 2022 three-tier panchayat elections were held without OBC reservation, while seats earmarked for the category were converted into unreserved constituencies.
“The state could not implement the 27% OBC quota in the 2022 panchayat elections as the provision was challenged before the high court on the ground that the mandatory triple test exercise had not been completed. Faced with legal hurdles, the govt withdrew the quota before the polls,” Naik added.
Officials said a final decision will depend on compliance with the legal requirements laid down by the apex court.
